chunks: You said: I was dragged like a camel with a nose string until I swore allegiance,
By the Eternal Allāh, you had intended to revile me but you have praised me, and to humiliate me but have yourself been humiliated!
What humiliation does it mean for a Muslim to be the victim of oppression so long as he does not entertain any doubt in his religion, nor any misgiving in his firm belief!
This argument of mine is intended for others, but I have stated it to you only in so far as it was appropriate.

key_terms.الْجَمَلُ الْـمَخْشُوشُ: a camel with a rope through its nose, used for leading

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali respond to Muawiya's claim of being forced to pledge allegiance?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) refutes Mu'awiya's claim of forced allegiance by distinguishing between physical coercion and spiritual integrity, asserting that oppression is not shameful unless it compromises one's faith. This response highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and the preservation of *yaqin* (certainty) as the true markers of leadership, turning Mu'awiya's intended humiliation into a testament of Ali's enduring authority. The letter serves as a foundational text for understanding the political theology of the early Caliphate, where legitimacy is rooted in divine certainty rather than mere political control.

en.sayed-ali-raza: You have said that I was dragged like a camel with a nose string to swear allegiance (to Abū Bakr at Saqīfah).
By the Eternal Allāh, you had intended to revile me but you have praised me, and to humiliate me but have yourself been humiliated.
What humiliation does it mean for a Muslim to be the victim of oppression so long as he does not entertain any doubt in his religion, nor any misgiving in his firm belief!
This argument of mine is intended for others, but I have stated it to you only in so far as it was appropriate.
